clue.text: Island fellow in lead, one involved in Paris production

indicators.note: in lead says the fellow goes at the front, ahead of the island

parts.note: HE is crossword shorthand for a man or fellow
Cuba is the Caribbean island

explanation.surface: A man from some island takes a leading role in a stage show staged in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paris production' looks theatrical, but Paris is the Trojan prince and his 'production' means the woman who produced him: Hecuba, Queen of Troy, was his mother.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend the Trojan queen bore Paris, so she is literally involved in producing him.

clue.text: Meat product an English essayist talked R about

indicators.note: talked about says the essayist's name is spoken and a similar-sounding word is wanted
talked about says the essayist's name is spoken and a similar-sounding word is wanted

parts.note: William Hazlitt was an English essayist of the Romantic era

explanation.surface: A butcher's product was the subject of conversation by an English writer.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as filed carries a stray 'R' from the newspaper scan, ignored here. Haslet is a British pork meatloaf, especially from Lincolnshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Haslet is a traditional British loaf of seasoned pork offal, a cold cooked meat.

clue.text: Song about a bauble with changing lustre K H CROW

indicators.note: about says the song goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a chant is a simple song or intoned melody
a bauble is a trinket or toy

explanation.surface: A tune is sung about a trinket that shimmers in the light.
explanation.walkthrough: The filed clue ends with OCR debris ('K H CROW') from the newspaper page, not part of the clue. Chatoyant describes the shifting sheen of a cat's eye gemstone.
explanation.definitionFit: Chatoyant is a gemmological term for stones whose sheen shifts like a cat's eye as they move.

clue.text: Composer displaying ecstatic joy

definitions.meaning: Sir Arthur ... was an English composer and Master of the Queen's Music

explanation.surface: A musician shows his delight at his work.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Bliss wrote music for films and ballets; the common noun means perfect happiness or rapture.

clue.text: Not the first journalist to be temporarily transferred!

parts.note: what comes after the first is the second
ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter is moved to another post for a while, and not for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: Seconding is the British practice of lending an employee to another department or organisation for a fixed period.
explanation.definitionFit: To second someone is to move them to other duties for a limited time, a British usage.

clue.text: Wise old politician deals with matters craftily in a short space

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters sit inside the short space

parts.note: an en is a printer's space half the width of an em

indicators.note: craftily suggests the letters are artfully worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A sage statesman handles affairs cunningly in very little room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craftily' rearranges DEALS and MATTERS into LDERSTATESMA, and 'in' places that inside EN, the printer's short space.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior politician respected for long experience and wisdom is called an elder statesman, an idiom.

clue.text: Huge vehicle crossing cape is being sent to Coventry

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing size

indicators.note: crossing says the vehicle stretches across the other pieces, holding them

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle running on rails
C is the map abbreviation for cape
taken as written

explanation.surface: A giant vehicle goes over a headland while someone is shunned.
explanation.walkthrough: The filed clue has a stray 'E' from the scan. 'Sent to Coventry' is a British idiom meaning deliberately ignored by everyone. 'crossing' puts C and IS between OS + TRA and M.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sent to Coventry means being shunned by everybody, which is exclusion from society.

clue.text: Order I stick up over entrance to club

indicators.note: over in a down clue says the first part sits above the next
up in a down clue says the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
a rod is a stick

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: I put up a notice by the doorway of a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses I + ROD to give DORI. Doric is one of the classical orders of architecture.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric is one of the classical orders of architecture, alongside Ionic and Corinthian.

clue.text: Make men pick up cart that's next to Uncle Sam's house

definitions.text: that's next to Uncle Sam's house

parts.note: to do something is to make it
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: pick up in a down clue says the cart is raised, read upwards

parts.note: a dray is a heavy cart

explanation.surface: Get the soldiers to collect a wagon standing beside an American home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pick up' reverses DRAY to give YARD. Uncle Sam is the United States, where a dooryard is the yard by a house door.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage the yard just outside a house's door is called by this compound name.

clue.text: In the country, old man eats acceptable fowl with mint on top

indicators.note: on top in a down clue says the new piece stands above the fowl
eats says the father takes the next piece inside

parts.note: papa is a father, an old man
U means upper-class, socially acceptable
mint condition is brand new
a guinea is short for guinea fowl

explanation.surface: Out in the country, a father dines on a fine bird garnished with mint.
explanation.walkthrough: U for 'acceptable' is the old upper-class versus non-U distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: The state occupying the eastern half of the island of New Guinea is a country in Oceania.

clue.text: Extremists in Westminster acquire territory that's in Africa

indicators.note: in says the extremes go inside the postcode

parts.note: SW1 is the London postcode of Westminster, the 1 read as I
A and Z are the extremes of the alphabet, A to Z
to land something is to acquire it

explanation.surface: Radicals in Parliament grab land in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: SW1 is the postal district covering Westminster, home of the UK Parliament; the digit 1 stands for I.
explanation.definitionFit: The southern African kingdom, now Eswatini, was long known by this name.

clue.text: Part of body originally training soldiers in this way

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the next word

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are soldiers
so means in this way or thus

explanation.surface: Soldiers' bodies are shaped by training like this.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the human body, without head or limbs, is called the torso.

clue.text: European with dynamism and self-esteem

parts.note: go means energy or dynamism

explanation.surface: A European full of energy and confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Ego is a person's sense of self-importance or self-worth.

clue.text: Landowners coy about papers a Catholic collected

indicators.note: about says the shy word goes around the rest
collected says the papers, a and Catholic are gathered in by the shy word

parts.note: coy means bashful or shy
a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper
RC is short for Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: Bashful property owners gather up documents for a Catholic.
explanation.walkthrough: The squirearchy is the class of landed gentry, squires collectively.
explanation.definitionFit: The squires of a district taken together, the landed gentry, form this collective class.

clue.text: Dull member of upper chamber given a hearing

indicators.note: given a hearing says the word is spoken and a soundalike is wanted

parts.note: a baron sits in the House of Lords, the upper chamber

explanation.surface: A tedious peer in the Lords gets his chance to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren can mean dull or unproductive, lacking interest or ideas.

clue.text: Take back son kept by model in topless minute, gown

indicators.note: in says the posing group goes inside the gown
topless says the top letter of the gown is removed

parts.note: a dress is a gown

indicators.note: kept by says the son is held inside the model

parts.note: to pose is to model

explanation.surface: A son is detained by a fashion model wearing a scanty little dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept by' puts S in POSE to give POSSE; 'topless' cuts DRESS to RESS; 'in' puts POSSE inside, after RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To repossess is to take back goods, typically when payments have not been made.

clue.text: Tourist requires lorry to cross river

indicators.note: to cross says the lorry goes over, around the river

parts.note: a tipper is a lorry that tips its load

explanation.surface: A traveller needs a truck to get over a river.
explanation.walkthrough: A tripper is British for a day-tripper, a holidaymaker on an outing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripper is a person on a pleasure trip, a sightseer or holidaymaker.

clue.text: Dry feed for automatic dispenser

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a vender is a vending machine dispensing goods

explanation.surface: Fodder for a vending machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Provender is fodder such as hay or grain for livestock.

clue.text: Precise copper in a decrepit car

indicators.note: in says the copper sits inside the old car

parts.note: a crate is slang for a battered old car
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police officer sits in a clapped-out car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate means exact or precise, free from error.

clue.text: Dupe taking part of one of Macavity's supporters …

definitions.meaning: a person used as a tool by another
Macavity is T. S. Eliot's mystery cat, who stands on its feet

explanation.surface: A fool joins in with one of a famous cat's feet.
explanation.walkthrough: Macavity is the criminal cat in T. S. Eliot's Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats; his supporters are his paws.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone used to do another's dirty work is a cat's paw, from the fable of the monkey and the cat.

clue.text: … it's beaten Macavity, say, more than once

indicators.note: more than once says the cat word is repeated

parts.note: Macavity is an example of a cat, and a male cat is a tom

explanation.surface: Macavity, the cat, keeps on getting thrashed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tom-tom is a drum, played by beating it with the hands.

clue.text: A little wife is typically full of fighting spirit

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A small wife is usually spirited.
explanation.definitionFit: Feisty means spirited and combative, ready for a fight.

clue.text: Manifest dude is using at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dandy is clearly using the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifest means plain to see, not hidden or disguised in any way.

clue.text: Black bishop in costly clothing

indicators.note: in says the bishop goes inside the costly word
clothing says the costly word dresses, surrounds, the bishop

parts.note: dear means costly
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A black-robed bishop in expensive vestments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black' as a verb means to ban or boycott, as in blacking goods in a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: To black something, as a union might, is to bar or exclude it, the same as debarring.

clue.text: Dump in channel

definitions.meaning: to abandon or get rid of something
a trench dug to carry water

explanation.surface: Rubbish thrown in a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: To get rid of is to ditch; a long narrow trench for drainage is a ditch.

clue.text: One may be glad when it's given by a wooer

definitions.text: One may be glad when it's given by a wooer

parts.words: One may be glad when it's given by a wooer
parts.note: the glad version of this is a flirtatious look a suitor gives

explanation.surface: Someone is delighted at a gift from a suitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'glad' looks like happiness, but the phrase is the idiom for an amorous glance.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone the glad eye means looking at them flirtatiously.

clue.text: Physician enters earlier regularly, having a stroll

indicators.note: enters says the physician goes inside
regularly takes every other letter of the word

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a physician's degree

explanation.surface: A doctor comes in early, having walked there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks ALE from the even letters of 'earlier'; MB goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An amble is a leisurely walk, a gentle stroll.

clue.text: Flowing in at speed, they also flow out

indicators.note: flowing suggests the letters are in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: Water comes in fast, and also goes out again.
explanation.definitionFit: Neap tides are the smallest tides of the month, which ebb as well as flow.

clue.text: Old person beginning to educate king in Italian

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of the next word
in says the king goes inside the Italian

parts.note: a Tuscan is an Italian from Tuscany
R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An elderly man starts to teach a monarch in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Etruscans were an ancient people of central Italy, preceding the Romans.
explanation.definitionFit: An Etruscan was a member of the ancient people of Etruria, so an old person indeed.

clue.text: Loveliest of trees a Greyfriars boy identified

definitions.meaning: the opening of A. E. Housman's poem about a blossoming tree
A pupil at Greyfriars School in Frank Richards' Billy Bunter stories

explanation.surface: The prettiest tree is linked to a schoolboy.
explanation.walkthrough: Housman's poem in A Shropshire Lad begins 'Loveliest of trees, the cherry now'. Greyfriars is the fictional school of the Billy Bunter stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Housman named the cherry as loveliest of trees; Bob Cherry is a Greyfriars boy.
